 Badambadi Police Station/ Opposite Party No.3 for  issuing necessary instructions to the Branch Manager,
 Union Bank of India, Malgodown Branch/ Opposite Party  No.4 and the Branch Manager, State Bank of India, City  Branch, Cuttack/ Opposite Party No.5 for de-freezing his  bank accounts in question.

. 3. Learned counsel for the Petitioner submits that the  Petitioner has been arrayed as an accused in G.R Case  No. 54 of 2022 arising out of of Badambadi PS Case No.

complaint filed by one Niranjan Panigrahi alleging that the Petitioner and his son and daughter-in-law formed a society, named, Jai Jhadeswar Cooperative Society Ltd.
situated at Baral Lane, Badambadi, Cuttack.
The said society has been registered on 23.11.2002 vide Registration No. 04CD with the IGR as Self-Help Cooperative Cuttack Division.

They persuaded the public to make transaction with their society with a promise to give higher rate of interest against investment in fixed deposit scheme, which would be more than the interest of any Nationalized Bank.
Being allured, the informant deposited Rs.10,60,000/- in 2008 in the fixed deposit scheme.
But, when the informant asked them for return of the said money on maturity which was invested back in the year 2008, the accused persons threatened him of dire consequences.

On such allegations, Badambadi PS Case No. 16 of 2022 was registered under Section 420,506,34 of IPC against the Petitioner, Shiva Kumar Swain (Son), Laxmi Priya Swain (Daughter-in-law).
4. Based on the FIR, the Police conducted investigation and during course of investigation, on 08.07.2022 , the police made requisition to the Opposite Party Nos.4 & 5 to freeze the bank accounts of the Petitioner.
5. It is relevant to state here that the Petitioner has been alleged to be a consultant of the Jai Jhadeswar Cooperative Society Ltd.

Thus, the Investigating Authority implicated the Petitioner for the alleged offences and linking the Petitioner to the operations of Jai Jhadeswar Cooperative Society Ltd. freezed the accounts of the Petitioner.

On 21.08.2022, the Police submitted charge sheet Upendra Nath Swain vs State Of Odisha & Ors. ..... Opposite ... on 11 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45346797/
2 against Shiva Kumar Swain (Son of the Petitioner) for the offences under Sections 420,409, 506, 34 IPG finding prima facie involvement of said Shiv Kumar Swain in the alleged offences citing him as the Chief Executive of

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Jai Jhadeswar Cooperative Society Ltd.
Till date the Petitioner has not been shown as an accused and no charge sheet against him has been filed.

The Police during investigation had asked for information regarding the office bearers of Jai Jhadeswar Cooperative Society Ltd.
from Asst. Registrar of Cooperative Societies, Cuttack.

Pursuant to the requisition, by its letter No.
294 dated 22.03.2022 the Police had submitted a report wherein it has specifically been mentioned that the Petitioner was not holding any official post in the said Jai Jhadeswar Cooperative Society Ltd.

This report of the Competent Authority further makes it clear that the Petitioner has been falsely added to the whole alleged occurrence though he is not connected in any manner with the Co-operative Society and its transactions.
The Petitioner is a Chartered Accountant and has independent source of Income.

But the Investigating Officer without verifying the source of income and the inflow of money to the Petitioner's account arbitrarily has given a direction to freeze the bank accounts of he Petitioner.

6. As the Investigation had already concluded and the Petitioner's bank accounts have been frozen since 08.07.2022 for more than 2.5 years, the Petitioner moved an application under Section 457 CrPC. for de-freezement of the Bank accounts vide Crl. Misc. Case No. 33 of 2024 before learned JMFC (City) Court, Cuttack.

In the said petition, it was categorically narrated that the Petitioner is a CA and has earned Rs.80,00,000/- from his independent practice which has commenced from the year 2000 after he voluntarily retired from service as Chief Manager of Andhra Bank from 1982 to 2000.
Apart from the above, he has also received an amount of Rs.50,40,000/- by selling his landed property.
Thus, there was no nexus between the Petitioner's account and Jai Jhadeswar Cooperative Society Ltd.

Pursuant to the application for defreezement of the account, the learned JMFC (City),
Cuttack called for a report from the Opposite Pary No.3 regarding requirement of the Petitioner's account for investigation and freezing.
The Opposite Pary No.3 vide letter dated 30.12.2024 informed the learned JMFC that the accounts of the Petitioner are no longer required to be freezed for further investigation of the case.

However, learned JMFC (City) Cuttack without appreciating aforesaid facts rejected the Petition of the Petitioner on flimsy ground and irrational premises that due to the gravity of offences the de-freezing of account cannot be permitted at present.
Hence, this Writ Petition.

7. Considering the facts & submissions made, since the investigation is already over, this Writ Petition stands disposed of directing the Opposite Party Nos.4 & 5/Bank to defreeze the account of the Petitioner within a period of one week from the date of presentation of this order.
8. Accordingly, the Writ Petition stands disposed of.
(Dr. S.K. Panigrahi) Judge Gitanjali Upendra Nath Swain vs State Of Odisha & Ors.
